div.div:
Read by network function
L1 carries bits; L2 forwards frames; L3 routes IP; L4 carries TCP/UDP; L5–L7 describe session, representation and application functions. These OSI numbers differ from the five hosting bands in the stack preview. The physical and access views own connectivity and request paths.

stack preview. The physical and access views own connectivity and request paths.

div.div:
Products span layers
Tailscale carries IP at L3 over WireGuard, normally using UDP; relays may carry encrypted traffic when direct connectivity is unavailable. Its API proxy is L7. The depicted Cloudflare web proxy uses an outbound Tunnel connection: QUIC/UDP 7844 or HTTP/2/TCP 7844. No inbound management port forwarding is proposed.

div.div:
Tailscale homelab choices
A supported host can run its own client. A subnet router extends access to selected LAN CIDRs; route approval and access policy are separate requirements. An Operator Connector can provide that router, but an in-cluster connector is not independent recovery. API proxy and subnet routing are separate roles, not consecutive mandatory hops.

div.div:
Not yet selected
No VLAN IDs, subnets, addresses, firewall implementation or CNI routing mode are chosen. A switch may also support L3 features, but none are selected here. L5/L6 are teaching analogies for modern protocols, not claims of dedicated OSI implementations. Cilium L7 policy is not selected by this view.
